title: Derivatives and Hedging - ASC 815
learning_objectives: Account for derivatives at fair value
Apply hedge accounting: fair value, cash flow, net investment

three_characteristics.explanation: Has underlying (price, rate, index) and notional amount (units specified), OR payment provision based on underlying
Requires no initial net investment or smaller than required for other contracts with similar response to market changes
Can be settled net, or provides for delivery of asset that puts recipient in position not substantially different from net settlement

basic_accounting.measurement: ALL derivatives measured at FAIR VALUE on balance sheet
basic_accounting.gains_losses_default: Changes in FV recognized in NET INCOME each period (unless designated as hedge and qualifies for hedge accounting)
basic_accounting.balance_sheet: Derivative asset (if positive FV) or Derivative liability (if negative FV)

hedge_accounting.purpose: Match timing of derivative gains/losses with hedged item to avoid income statement volatility
qualification_requirements: Formal documentation of hedging relationship at inception
Hedge must be highly effective (offset 80-125% of hedged risk)
Effectiveness assessed at inception and ongoing
Hedged item must be specifically identified

three_types.hedged_item: Exposure to changes in FV of recognized asset/liability or firm commitment
three_types.accounting: BOTH derivative AND hedged item adjusted to FV with changes in INCOME (gains/losses offset)
three_types.result: Derivative G/L and hedged item G/L both in income, largely offset if highly effective
three_types.example_entry:
DR Derivative Asset $XXX
   CR Gain on Derivative $XXX

DR Loss on Hedged Item $XXX
   CR Hedged Item $XXX

three_types.hedged_item: Exposure to variability in cash flows of recognized asset/liability or forecasted transaction
three_types.accounting: Derivative to FV with EFFECTIVE portion of gain/loss in OCI. Ineffective portion in income. Reclassify OCI to income when hedged transaction affects income.
three_types.result: Smooths income by deferring derivative G/L in OCI until hedged transaction impacts income
three_types.example_entry:
DR Derivative Asset $100
   CR OCI - Cash Flow Hedge $80 (effective)
   CR Gain on Derivative $20 (ineffective)

three_types.hedged_item: Foreign currency exposure of net investment in foreign operation
examples: Forward contract to hedge investment in foreign subsidiary
three_types.accounting: Similar to cash flow hedge - effective portion in OCI (cumulative translation adjustment), ineffective in income
three_types.result: Offsets foreign currency translation adjustments on foreign subsidiary

fair_value: Adjust to FV, change in income

embedded_derivatives.definition: Derivative implicitly or explicitly contained in another contract (hybrid instrument)
examples: Convertible bonds (conversion option is embedded derivative)
embedded_derivatives.bifurcation_test: Separate embedded derivative from host contract if:
bifurcation_criteria: Economic characteristics not clearly and closely related to host
Hybrid instrument not measured at FV through income
Separate instrument with same terms would be derivative
embedded_derivatives.if_bifurcated: Account for embedded derivative at FV through income, host contract under normal rules

effectiveness_testing.highly_effective: Hedge must offset 80-125% of hedged item's changes attributable to hedged risk
effectiveness_testing.testing_frequency: At inception and ongoing (at least quarterly)
effectiveness_testing.if_not_effective: Discontinue hedge accounting prospectively, reclassify amounts in OCI per guidance

cpa_exam_strategies.identification: Three characteristics for derivative: underlying/notional, little initial investment, net settlement
cpa_exam_strategies.default_accounting: ALL derivatives at FV. Default = changes in income (unless designated hedge)
cpa_exam_strategies.hedge_types: Fair value hedge = both in income. Cash flow hedge = effective part in OCI. Look for 'forecasted' or 'variable' = cash flow.
cpa_exam_strategies.most_tested: Fair value vs. cash flow hedge distinction. Know where G/L go (income vs. OCI).

key_points: Derivatives = FV with changes in income (default)
Hedge accounting matches derivative G/L with hedged item timing
Fair value hedge: Both derivative and hedged item G/L in income
Cash flow hedge: Effective portion of derivative G/L in OCI, reclassify when hedged transaction affects income
Qualification: Documentation, highly effective (80-125%), specific identification
Embedded derivatives: Separate if not clearly/closely related and not FV through income
